section.title: Push
section.p: Use: Sends local commits from the current branch to the remote repository.

Details: A push publishes commits that exist in your local repository but not yet on the remote branch. Other users can then pull those commits. If the local branch does not have a corresponding remote branch, the Git Client creates a remote branch with the same name automatically.
Scope: Current branch in the selected working copy.

ul.li: Git Branch Manager view contextual menu.

section.title: Pull
section.p: Use: Opens a submenu with actions for bringing changes from the remote repository into the local repository.

Details: Pull updates your local branch with commits from a remote branch. Depending on the selected strategy, Git either merges the remote changes into your branch or rebases your local unpublished commits on top of the updated remote state. The pull action that you use from the drop-down menu becomes the default action of the toolbar button.
Scope: Current branch in the selected working copy.

ul.li: Pull drop-down menu in the Git Staging view toolbar.

section.title: Pull (Merge)
section.p: Use: Pulls the latest changes from the remote repository and merges them into the local branch.

Details: A merge keeps your local commits and the remote commits as separate history lines when both sides changed. If needed, Git creates a merge commit that records how the two histories were joined. If the same files were changed in incompatible ways, Git reports conflicts that must be resolved before the merge can finish.
Scope: Current branch and its tracked remote branch.

ul.li: Git Branch Manager view contextual menu.

section.title: Pull (Rebase)
section.p: Use: Pulls the latest changes from the remote repository, then reapplies local unpublished commits on top of the updated branch.

Details: Rebase creates a linear history by moving your local commits so they appear after the commits pulled from the remote branch. Because this rewrites local commit history, use it only for commits that have not been shared. If conflicts occur, resolve them and then continue the rebase.
Best Practice: Use rebase only when your team workflow allows it for unpublished local commits.

ul.li: Git Branch Manager view contextual menu.

section.title: Pull...
section.p: Use: Pulls changes from a remote branch other than the one being tracked by the current local branch.

Details: The dialog box lets you choose the remote branch and the pull strategy: merge or rebase. Use this action when the current branch must receive changes from a specific remote branch that is not its configured tracking branch.
Scope: Selected remote branch and current local branch.

section.title: Resolve Using Mine
section.p: Use: Resolves a conflicted file by keeping the local version.
Details: In a conflict, Mine means the version from your current local branch. This action marks the selected file as resolved with your local content and discards the incoming version for that file.
Caution: Use this action only when the incoming version is not needed.
Accessible From: Contextual menu of a conflicted file in the Unstaged files area.

section.title: Resolve Using Theirs
section.p: Use: Resolves a conflicted file by keeping the incoming version.

Details: In a conflict, Theirs means the version being brought into your branch by the merge or rebase. This action marks the selected file as resolved with the incoming content and discards your local version for that file.
Caution: Use this action only when your local version is not needed.
Accessible From: Contextual menu of a conflicted file in the Unstaged files area.

section.title: Mark as Resolved
section.p: Use: Marks a conflicted file as resolved after you edit the file and choose which changes to keep.

Details: Git cannot finish a merge or rebase while files remain in a conflicted state. After you resolve the conflict markers or use the compare editor to choose the correct content, this action tells Git that the file is ready for the next step.
Best Practice: Use this action only after you check the merged file content.
Accessible From: Contextual menu of a conflicted file in the Unstaged files area.

section.title: Resolve with AI
section.p: Use: Uses AI Positron to analyze a conflicted file and propose a resolution.
Details: The action opens a review dialog with an explanation and an AI-generated resolved version that you can review before applying.
Availability: Available for conflicted files. Requires the Positron AI Assistant add-on.
Accessible From: Resolve Conflict submenu in the contextual menu of a conflicted file in the Unstaged files area.

section.title: Abort Merge
section.p: Use: Stops the current merge operation and restores the repository to its state before the merge started.

Details: Abort merge is useful when a merge produces conflicts that you do not want to resolve now. Git cancels the merge operation and returns the working copy to the pre-merge state as far as possible.
Scope: Current repository merge operation.
Accessible From: Conflict resolution controls shown during a merge conflict.

section.title: Restart Merge
section.p: Use: Restarts the current merge so you can resolve the conflicts again from the beginning.
Details: Use this action when you want to discard the current conflict-resolution attempt and return the merge to its initial conflicted state.
Scope: Current repository merge operation.
Accessible From: Conflict resolution controls shown during a merge conflict.

section.title: Continue Rebase
section.p: Use: Continues the current rebase after conflicts are resolved.

Details: During a rebase, Git may stop when it cannot apply a local commit cleanly on top of the updated branch. After you resolve and mark the conflicted files, this action tells Git to continue replaying the remaining local commits.
Scope: Current repository rebase operation.
Accessible From: Conflict resolution controls shown during a rebase conflict.

section.title: Abort Rebase
section.p: Use: Stops the current rebase operation and restores the repository to its state before the rebase started.

Details: Abort rebase is useful when you do not want to continue resolving rebase conflicts. Git cancels the rebase and returns the branch to the commit where it was before the rebase operation began.
Scope: Current repository rebase operation.
Accessible From: Conflict resolution controls shown during a rebase conflict.

section.title: Abort Cherry-Pick
section.p: Use: Stops the current cherry-pick operation and restores the repository to its state before the cherry-pick started.
Details: Abort cherry-pick is useful when a cherry-pick produces conflicts that you do not want to resolve now.
Scope: Current repository cherry-pick operation.
Accessible From: Conflict resolution controls shown during a cherry-pick conflict.

section.title: Abort Revert
section.p: Use: Stops the current revert operation and restores the repository to its state before the revert started.
Details: Abort revert is useful when a revert produces conflicts that you do not want to resolve now.
Scope: Current repository revert operation.
Accessible From: Conflict resolution controls shown during a revert conflict.
